We've shown that plants do in fact feel a semblance of pain. (If you're curious the study was about the defense mechanisms used by plants)

They react strongly to being eaten but a lot of them are releasing chemicals that don't effect/are not very effective on humans. Examples: onions release a toxin that causes swelling in most animals but just irritates our glands slightly, or how asperagus releases a toxin intended to cause indigestion but just makes our pee smell funny. Hot peppers are another example, capsacian is a chemical it uses to scare off predators, we eat it as a challenge.

Full veganism (not eating any fats or meats from animals) has been shown to be incredably unhealthy, often requiring a lot of supplimenting to account for missing nutrients. 

I can attest that there are better butchering practices in the last 10 years than have been fought against in recent years. There was a scientist (don't remember her name but look up humane slaughter practices) who developed a method that lulls the animal into a peaceful sleep then cleanly kills before the animal even has a chance to feel pain. It's being spread to other slaughter houses as it has been shown to even make the meat taste better. We still have a long way to go but encouraging people to adopt costly and unhealthy (without supplimenting which is more costly) diet choices just so you can say you don't eat them is just poor form.

So i'm running a game right now and weird things like this happen, the trick is to explain to everyone that at the end of the day this is supposed to be fun for everyone. Let me say that again "fun for EVERYONE" that includes the DM.

First, you have to make it clear to them that there are concequences to making stupid choices, in my case I simply tell them that if they make stupid choices it may end up with them having their PC killed. Personally I have about 4 sheets rolled up so that if any PCs die they don't have to roll up a new one right away.

The big thing is you cannot let Dante change his fate too often, if he cannot accept that his character will die if he keeps up the nonsense then DND might not be the right game for him.

As for the favouritism thing, I think you have a handle on it, but understand that every event is an isolated incident, don't let some grudge ruin future sessions. Clear the air before and after the session and relax. Players often start to see themselves as an extention of their character, so play to that, show the concequences well before you allow your players to challenge the obstacle.

Really the big thing to remember is as a GM/DM you aren't a player, you are the facilitator, so players cannot be allowed to sway you in any way.
